_comment: Learn step by step (/step-by-step): the curated beginner path. Tasks reference reviewed items by ref, they never copy text — see src/lib/einfach-content.js for the ref formats and docs/easy-mode-tier1-v1.md for how to add a unit. Check with: pnpm check:einfach. Grammar order follows grammatik-lehrplan.json (English A1 order: be, articles, plurals, possessives, present simple, questions, object pronouns, imperatives, prepositions of time, was/were). English version (beginner-path run, 2026-10-29): A1, A2 and B1 are playable, units in the lehrplan order of their grammar topic; they use only sources that are already English (grammar topics and akkusativ.json); word, article (der/die/das), phrase, listening and speaking tasks come back when the vocab, speaking, listening and pronunciation items have made their sources English. Postcards with source "neu" are facts written for this path and still need Edgar's check.

units.title: Introduce yourself
claims: You say who you are and where you are from.
You use I am, you are, she is.

postcard.fact: Big Ben is not the tower. It is the big bell inside the tower.

tasks.hint: Which form of be goes with I?
She is one person. He, she and it have the same form.
Amira is a woman.
A question with be: Are comes first.
We is more than one person. We, you and they have the same form.
Priya and Liam are two people.
Say what your sister does.

units.title: Show someone your home
claims: You talk about the things in your home.
You choose a, an or the.

postcard.fact: Edinburgh Castle stands on the rock of an old volcano.

tasks.hint: Say “old” out loud. Is the first sound a vowel?
Say “big” out loud. Is the first sound a vowel?
We both know which door.
tasks.why: We know which door: the door of this room. So: the.

tasks.hint: Apple starts with a vowel sound.
Cats in general, not one cat.
tasks.why: Plural in general: no article. I like cats.

tasks.hint: Say “hour”. Do you hear the h?
tasks.why: The h in hour is silent. The first sound is a vowel, so: an hour.

tasks.hint: Breakfast, lunch, dinner: meals in general.
tasks.why: Meals have no article: have lunch, have breakfast.

units.title: Go shopping
claims: You say how many things you want.
You make plurals: one apple, two apples.

postcard.fact: Cardiff is the capital of Wales. Many signs there are in Welsh and English.

tasks.hint: One potato, six … Watch the spelling.
tasks.why: potato → potatoes. Some words with -o add -es.

tasks.hint: Bus ends in -s. Then you add -es.
One sandwich, two … After -ch you add -es.
Shoes: more than one.
One knife, four … The f changes.
One child, two … This plural is irregular.
City ends in a consonant + y. The y changes.

units.title: Talk about your family
claims: You talk about your family.
You say my, his, her and Tom's.

postcard.fact: The Titanic was built in Belfast.

tasks.hint: Kwame is a man. The owner decides.
Mei is a woman. The owner decides, not the brother.
Carlos is a man. The owner decides, not the sister.
The coat belongs to my sister.
tasks.why: One owner: add 's. my sister's coat.

tasks.hint: The keys belong to my parents. Parents already ends in -s.
tasks.why: Plural with -s: add only '. my parents' keys.

tasks.hint: Priya is a woman.

units.title: Talk about your day
claims: You say what you do every day.
You add -s after he, she and it.

postcard.fact: In Bath, warm water comes up from under the ground. The Romans built baths there.

tasks.hint: My dad = he. Watch the spelling.
The train = it.
With I, the verb has no -s.
He + brush. After -sh you add -es.
I, you, we, they: don't.
Priya = she.
Zofia = she. Study ends in a consonant + y.

units.title: In a café
claims: You ask yes/no questions: Do you…? Is it…?
You give short answers: Yes, I do.

postcard.fact: In York you can walk on the old city walls.

tasks.hint: The question starts with Do.
The question starts with Is.
Make a question. Like is a main verb, and the subject is you.
tasks.why: You + a main verb (like): the question starts with Do. Do you like pizza?

tasks.hint: Ask politely for help: Can you …
The question starts with Does. For no, add n't.
Make a question from: They live in Cardiff.
The question starts with Is. For no, add n't.

units.title: Get to know someone
claims: You ask: Who? Where? When? How old?
You ask people where they live.

postcard.fact: The Beatles came from Liverpool.

tasks.hint: The answer is a place.
The answer is a person.
Ask about the place: Where + do + you …
There is no main verb after the subject. Use be.
The answer is an age.
The answer is a time.
Ask about a number: How many + brothers …

units.title: Say what you like
claims: You say what you like: I like it.
You use me, him, her, it, us, them.

postcard.fact: Oxford has the oldest university in the English-speaking world.

tasks.hint: The phone is one thing.
Tom is a man. After the verb, use the object form.
My parents: more than one person, after the verb.
Help who? The object form of I.
The children: more than one. After at, use the object form.
My book is one thing.

units.title: Ask the way
claims: You understand directions: Turn left at the bank.
You tell people what to do and not do.

postcard.fact: In Cambridge, lots of people go to work by bike.

tasks.hint: A command starts with the base verb.
Take away you. Keep the base verb.
A suggestion for you and me.
Ask politely. Please comes first.
To say what not to do, start with one word.
What not to do: Don't + base verb.
Start with the verb: Open …

units.title: Make an appointment
claims: You make an appointment on the phone.
You say: on Monday, at ten, in May.

postcard.fact: On a clear day, you can see France from Dover.

tasks.hint: Thursday is a day.
6.45 is a clock time.
May is a month.
4 September is a date.
Look at the word before tomorrow.
tasks.why: No preposition before tomorrow, today, next or last. See you tomorrow.

tasks.hint: First the day, then the clock time.
Careful: in the evening, but … night.

units.title: At the doctor's
claims: You understand instructions: Write your name here.
You say: Be careful. Don't be late.

postcard.fact: William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-upon-Avon in 1564.

tasks.hint: Start with the base verb.
A command has no -s and no to.
Careful is an adjective.
What not to be: Don't + be.
After Don't, use the base verb.
Quiet is an adjective.
What not to do: start with one word.

units.title: Say where you were
claims: You say where you were: I was at home.
You ask: Where were you? Was she there?

postcard.fact: Glasgow is the biggest city in Scotland.

tasks.hint: Which past form of be goes with I?
We: more than one person.
A question with Where.
Tom = he.
The shops: more than one.
A yes/no question: Was comes first.
He: one person.

units.title: Talk about your work
claims: You say what you are doing now.
You choose: I work or I am working.

postcard.fact: In 1948, one of the first computers ran its first program in Manchester.

tasks.hint: I + am + verb-ing.
They: are + verb-ing.
Shh! It is happening now.
Every day: a routine.
Short vowel + one consonant: double the consonant.
Want is a state verb. It has no -ing.
She is in the bathroom now.

units.title: Talk about your weekend
claims: You say what you did at the weekend.
You use went, saw, bought and didn't.

postcard.fact: Brighton has a long pier that goes out into the sea.

tasks.hint: Last summer: the past. Go is irregular.
See is irregular. I see it today, I … it yesterday.
tasks.why: see → saw. Seen is not the past simple: it needs have (I have seen).

tasks.hint: After didn't, use the base verb.
Go is irregular. The time word is last.
Short vowel + one consonant: double the consonant.
After Did, use the base verb.
Question word first, then did.

units.title: Say no
claims: You say what you don't do.
You use don't, doesn't, didn't and no.

postcard.fact: From Llanberis, a train goes up Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon), the highest mountain in Wales.

tasks.hint: I, and it is true now.
Zofia = she, and it is true now.
Last night: the past.
Time is a noun. no + noun.
After didn't, use the base verb.
She + doesn't + work …
Before a or an, use not.

units.title: Ask for permission
claims: You ask: Can I…? Do I have to…?
You say must, mustn't and don't have to.

postcard.fact: Loch Ness, near Inverness, holds more water than all the lakes in England and Wales together.

tasks.hint: You ask if it is OK to sit there.
It is not allowed.
He can sleep late: it is not necessary.
A question with have to: Does + she + have to …
She is three. She is not able to read.
In a question, can goes first.
It is necessary: have to + base verb.

units.title: Ask politely
claims: You ask politely: Could you…? Would you mind…?
You say I'd like instead of I want.

postcard.fact: People from Newcastle are often called Geordies.

tasks.hint: You say what you want, politely.
You offer something to someone.
After Would you mind, use -ing.
A request: Could + you + please + base verb.
Only one of these words goes with mind.

options: Would you like to some tea?
tasks.hint: Offer something politely: Would you like …?
tasks.why: Do you like tea? asks if you like it in general. To offer tea now: Would you like some tea?

tasks.hint: Very polite: Would you mind + -ing.

units.title: Say where things are
claims: You say where things are in a room.
You use in, on, at, next to, between.

postcard.fact: Land's End, near Penzance, is the far west of mainland England.

tasks.hint: A wall is a surface.
A kitchen is a room: you are inside it.
High up: higher than the door.
on + a surface · next to = right beside.
The bank on one side, the supermarket on the other.
When you sleep, you are … bed.
Floors in a building: like a surface.

units.title: Buy presents
claims: You say who you give something to.
You use to and for: buy it for her.

postcard.fact: The Clifton Suspension Bridge in Bristol opened in 1864.

tasks.hint: buy something for someone.
give something to someone.
After bought, use the object form of he.
give + person + thing.
The flowers: more than one.
It goes first, then to + person.
make something for someone.

units.title: Plan your day
claims: You use phrasal verbs: get up, turn off.
You put it in the middle: turn it off.

postcard.fact: Stonehenge, near Salisbury, is about 5,000 years old.

tasks.hint: You get out of bed.
A question about your morning.
It's cold: start to wear your coat.
Nobody is at home to watch it.
With it or them, the pronoun goes in the middle.
A polite request. The pronoun goes in the middle.
look for = try to find. Keep for after looking.

units.title: Tell a story
claims: You tell a story in the right order.
You use was doing and had done.

postcard.fact: In The Canterbury Tales, Geoffrey Chaucer wrote about people travelling to Canterbury.

tasks.hint: A long action was in progress. Then the phone rang.
The film started first, before I got there.
The long action: was cooking. The short event: rang.
A long action in the past, with we.
First the big lunch, later not hungry.
Leave is irregular.
A question about an action in progress last night.

units.title: Talk about when you were young
claims: You say what you used to do as a child.
You ask: Did you use to…?

postcard.fact: The poet Dylan Thomas was born in Swansea.

tasks.hint: Living in Leeds is a state. It is not true now.
After didn't, use the base form.
A question about the past.

options: Did you use to have a dog?
Did you used to have a dog?
Were you use to have a dog?
tasks.hint: Did + subject + use to + base verb.
Having a bike is a state, not an action.
Having a motorbike is a state.
An action that happened again and again.

units.title: Talk about plans
claims: You say what you are going to do.
You choose will, going to or -ing.

postcard.fact: Durham Cathedral is more than 900 years old.

tasks.hint: Mei = she.
It. You can see the snow coming.
will + base verb. No to, no -s.
The speaker decides right now.
It is booked. The time is fixed.
A plan: We're going to …
will + not = won't.

units.title: Chat with colleagues
claims: You say what you enjoy, want and hope.
You choose -ing or to + verb.

postcard.fact: Aberdeen is called the Granite City. Many buildings there are made of grey granite.

tasks.hint: Which pattern does enjoy take?
Which pattern does decide take?
Which pattern does finish take?
hope + to + verb.
Which pattern does mind take?

options: I don't want to go out.
I not want to go out.
tasks.hint: want + to + verb. The negative needs don't.
enjoy + -ing.

units.title: Describe people and things
claims: You describe people and things more exactly.
You use who, which, whose and where.

postcard.fact: Hadrian's Wall, near Carlisle, was built by the Romans more than 1,900 years ago.

tasks.hint: The woman is a person.
A song is a thing.
The bike belongs to the girl.
The shop is a place.

options: I met a man who plays in a band.
I met a man who he plays in a band.
I met a man which plays in a band.
tasks.hint: A person: who. Don't repeat he.
where: a place.
whose: the mother belongs to the friend.

units.title: Ask for information
claims: You ask politely: Could you tell me where…?
You use statement order after the question word.

postcard.fact: Windsor Castle is the oldest and largest castle in the world that people still live in.

tasks.hint: The direct question has a question word. Keep it.
A yes/no question has no question word.
After where: subject + verb. No does.
After what time: subject + verb. No does.
Direct question: Where is the breakfast room?
Look at the direct question. Keep its question word.
Direct question: How much does a double room cost?

units.title: Talk about a problem
claims: You use verbs with the right preposition.
You say: wait for, depend on, worry about.

postcard.fact: Keswick is in the Lake District. Scafell Pike, the highest mountain in England, is not far away.

tasks.hint: wait + …
depend + …
agree + … + a person.
worry + …
A question with depend + on.
listen + …
talk + about.

units.title: Describe a flat
claims: You describe a flat with several adjectives.
You put adjectives in the right order.

postcard.fact: Near Bushmills, the Giant's Causeway has about 40,000 stone columns.

tasks.hint: Opinion comes before age.
Age comes before material.
Size comes before shape.
Size comes before origin.
Colour comes before material.
Size comes before colour.
After your: age, then colour.
